alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 11:13AM MDT until October 23 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and river flooding caused by excessive rainfall
is expected.

* WHERE...South Central Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected, especially along the San
Juan River down to the Navajo River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1107 AM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected in the warned area.
Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen over the last 24
hours. Excess runoff from rainfall will cause the San Juan River
to rise downstream to the Navajo River, potentially inundating
homes.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
San Juan River, Blanco, Rio, Montezuma Creek and Navajo River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Juanita and Gato.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 10:26AM MDT until October 23 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
...The National Weather Service in Grand Junction CO has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Colorado...

San Juan River at Pagosa Springs affecting Archuleta County.

For the San Juan River...including Pagosa Springs...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Pagosa Springs.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 13.7 feet, Flooding of some residences near the river
around Pagosa Springs is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 8.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage late this
afternoon to 13.8 feet tomorrow morning. It will then fall below
flood stage tomorrow afternoon to 8.3 feet Saturday afternoon. It
will rise to 8.4 feet early Sunday morning. It will then fall
again and remain below flood stage.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 10:15AM MDT until October 23 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and Utah,
including the following areas, Arches/Grand Flat,
Canyonlands/Natural Bridges, La Sal and Abajo Mountains and
Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...Through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recent burn scars and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Flooding is likely with additional rounds of showers and
thunderstorms expected through Thursday night.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.title: Road Construction-150319
alerts.description: Between Frontage Road and County Road 232 (near Durango) from Mile Point 88 to Mile Point 89.5. Road construction. Starting Thursday at 7:00PM MDT until Friday, at about 7:00AM MDT. Full schedule below: • October 22, 7:00PM - October 23, 7:00AM Comment: The US 550-US 160 Grandview Interchange exit and entrance ramps will experience staggered nighttime closures from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., Sunday night through Friday morning. For more information email: resurfacingproject@gmail.com.

alerts.title: US 160 Pagosa Springs Reconstruction-147598
alerts.description: Between US 84 and Pike Drive (Pagosa Springs) from Mile Point 144.3 to Mile Point 141.8. Road construction. Starting October 22, 2026 at 7:00AM MDT until October 22, 2026 at about 6:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • October 22, 7:00AM - October 22, 6:00PM Comment: Harman Park & Piedra Road-Work is underway at this intersection of US 160. Working hours will be intermittent day and night so motorists should plan for potential delays, Monday-Saturday. Please allow extra time to get through the work zone. Safety benefits of this work includes pedestrian safety upgrades and ADA accessibility improvements. Expect lane shifts and up to 15-minute delays. Crews will switch two-way traffic into the eastbound lanes, perform temporary striping operations and begin asphalt milling in the westbound lanes. Parking will not be permitted on US 160 and vehicles will be towed at the owner's expense. Westbound lane closures, 10’ width and 75’ length restrictions will remain in place 24/7 through end of 2026. Work is weather-dependent. For questions contact the project team at 970-335-9230 or Pagosa160reconstruction@gmail.com Project Webpage: www.codot.gov/projects/us160pagosasprings
